scope: Coverage matrix (plan Step 6): retrieval-spec dimensions x pinned sources. Every frozen source is judged on every dimension (no empty cells; sources that do not report a quantity are marked unavailable with their trail). Verdicts restricted to covered/partial/unavailable where covered means the source reports values or a distribution that contains the dimension's retrieval value range. Coverage is NOT justification: no cell implies a default value is justified, and no recommendation column exists. Verdicts cite the source's own reported quantities; wavelength/pair mismatches are recorded as caveats and conversions live in derived_comparisons as machine-checkable worked examples.

dimension_source.note: Dimension values are referenced by json-path from this committed product; the schema gate test re-asserts equality against the live file.

branch_rule_status.note: The >0.625 volcanic/stratospheric branch rule is NOT triggered (pool max 0.184); no volcanic/stratospheric-perturbation sources were collected, by design of the spec itself.

cells.basis: Site-level observed tau ranges, tabulated at 440 nm (urban/biomass rows) and 1020 nm (dust/oceanic rows), not 550: Lanai (clean oceanic) 0.01<=tau1020<=0.2, mean 0.04; GSFC urban 0.1<=tau440<=1.0, mean 0.24. Ranges, not distributions. The Lanai row converted over the documented oceanic alpha range [0, 1.55] spans tau550 ~ [0.010, 0.521] as a MARGINAL ENVELOPE (worked examples lanai_low/lanai_high) - the ranges are not paired (low-AOD, alpha) joint observations. Within that envelope the pool's low end 0.0259 is contained only for alpha up to ~1.54 of [0, 1.55]; coverage of the June value is therefore conditional on the unobserved alpha of low-AOD samples and is not claimed unconditionally.

cells.basis: No collected source directly documents the spec's 0-10 km truncated exponential geometry with H = 8000 m. The CALIPSO H63 statistic (altitude below which 63% of column AOD lies) equals the exponential scale height only for an untruncated profile; converting the spec's 10-km-truncated layer to that metric gives an H63-equivalent of ~4775 m (worked example h63_target_layer in derived_comparisons[3]), which overlaps the observed H63 range's upper extreme (oceans ~1-2 km, most land 1.5-3 km, max ~4.5-5 km over deserts/elevated regions, Fig. 9 figure read; H63 is referenced to sea level so terrain elevation contributes). This comparison crosses definitions (truncated-layer integral vs full-column statistic) and cannot certify or exclude the profile shape, so it is recorded as context rather than as a coverage basis.
cells.location: sources.json winker2013_calipso_3d -> Sec. 5 + Fig. 9 (printed p. 3352); figure_read_caveat; worked example derived_comparisons[3]; search_log.md W3.1-W3.3 (classic standard-atmosphere reports blocked, trail recorded)

derived_comparisons.name: gsfc_distribution_summary
derived_comparisons.method: Percentiles computed from the pinned CSV (AERONET L2.0, -999 filtered): AOD_500nm n=6677 min 0.0222 P10 0.0535 P25 0.0767 median 0.1163 P75 0.2056 P90 0.3729 max 1.3022; AOD_440nm n=6680 min 0.0251 P10 0.0639 median 0.1404 P75 0.2511 P90 0.4524 max 1.4052; alpha(440-870) n=6683 min 0.206 P10 1.298 median 1.728 max 2.318. AOD_551/560 channels are empty in this export; AOD_500nm used as the near-550 channel.
derived_comparisons.pool_band_fraction: 71.3% of AOD500 retrievals inside [0.0259, 0.1839]; 0.2% below the floor.
derived_comparisons.dynamic_range_note: Site distribution P90/P10 = 0.3729/0.0535 = 6.97 - the same order as the pool ratio R=7.110; recorded as a magnitude comparison, not an explanation.

derived_comparisons.name: wavelength_conversions
derived_comparisons.formula: tau550 = tau_x * (550_nm / x_nm)^(-alpha)  (Angstrom law between the source's tabulated wavelength x_nm and 550 nm)
derived_comparisons.envelope_note: Each worked example composes a source's documented tau range with its documented alpha range into a MARGINAL ENVELOPE: the endpoints come from independent ranges, NOT from paired (low-AOD, alpha) joint observations. The alpha ranges are the sources' own documented site/type ranges used as a sensitivity span, not observations tied to the AOD extremes.

derived_comparisons.name: humidity_axis_vs_pool
derived_comparisons.statement: Full-axis growth dry->99%: x12.1-x18.6 for the three components with both endpoints pinned (SUSO x16.98, WASO x12.14, SSAM x18.58); SSCM's high end is pinned at 95% (x8.17) with 98/99 missing. 50%->99%: x7.4-x7.6 (WASO/SSAM). Moderate spans: 50->80% x1.49-x1.52, 50->90% x2.07-x2.17, 70->98% x3.92-x4.04. Pool ratio R=7.110. Magnitude comparison only.

derived_comparisons.name: geometry_h63_conversion
derived_comparisons.formula: h63 = -H * ln(1 - 0.63 * (1 - exp(-top/H)))  (altitude below which 63% of the truncated exponential layer's AOD lies, layer [0, top] with scale height H)
derived_comparisons.definition_caveat: CALIPSO's H63 is a full-column statistic referenced to sea level (terrain elevation contributes; polar high values stated spurious in the source). It equals the scale height only for an untruncated exponential. The conversion below puts the spec's truncated layer on the same metric for context; a match or mismatch of these single-number summaries does not certify or exclude the profile shape, and no source directly documents the spec's geometry.

worked_examples.source: retrieval_spec.layer_geometry (scale_height_m 8000, class 0-10 km exponential), converted to the H63 metric of winker2013_calipso_3d
